summary: Fire lookout tower on the summit of Mt. Kobau, removed in 2007; a 600 m trail now runs to the former tower site.

facts.status_note: Canada Lookouts dates the removal to 2007. BC Parks describes the summit spot as the location of the former lookout.

access.note: The main road to the summit is open to motor vehicles. The gravel roads are maintained infrequently.

visit.trail_note: Mount Kobau Lookout Trail climbs about 600 m from the summit parking area to where the former tower stood.

events.note: Canada Lookouts dates the removal of the lookout to 2007.
The Testalinden Creek fire left burned trees on the approach to the summit, according to a hiking blog. The blog does not say whether the lookout was affected.

evidence.supports: Mt. Kobau is one of four sites in the South Okanagan Grasslands Protected Area
evidence.quote: The protected area comprises four sites: Mt. Kobau, Kilpoola, Chopaka East and Chopaka West

evidence.supports: The trail starts at the summit parking lot and runs about 600 m to where the former tower stood
evidence.quote: There are 2 hiking trails accessible from the parking lot at the top of Mount Kobau. Mount Kobau Lookout Trail takes you 600 metres up to where the former fire lookout tower stood.

evidence.supports: BC Parks describes a viewpoint at the former lookout location with views over the Okanagan Valley, Osoyoos Lake and the Similkameen Valley
evidence.quote: The viewpoint at the location of the former fire lookout atop Mt. Kobau gives visitors a panorama of the Okanagan Valley, Osoyoos Lake and the Similkameen Valley.

evidence.supports: The main road to the summit is open to motor vehicles
evidence.quote: The main road to the summit of Mt. Kobau is open to motor vehicles, all other roads are closed.

evidence.supports: The road to the summit is gravel and maintained infrequently
evidence.quote: Both Kruger Mt. Rd. and the road to Mt. Kobau are gravel roads and maintained infrequently.

evidence.supports: Burned trees from the 2015 Testalinden Creek fire line the way to the summit
evidence.quote: You need to walk through the burned trees left from the devastation of the 2015 Testalinden Creek fire.

notes_for_editor: Only three sources, and none gives a build date, staffing or any fire history for the lookout itself. The only removal date is a one-line entry in a volunteer archive (Canada Lookouts). The BC Parks page supplies the trail, road and viewpoint facts. The brief status unknown is replaced by removed. A Castanet forum thread in search results (undated; the fetch returned HTTP 403) describes a boarded-up fire-watch hut on Mount Kobau. If that account is recent, it conflicts with a 2007 removal. It could not be read or cited, so the story does not mention it. The BC Parks data catalogue link in the brief returned no text (JavaScript page). Visit facts (summit road open to cars, 600 m trail) are from the BC Parks page as published and may have changed.
